claim.value: Patterns of discrepancies can constrain competing accounts of departures at distinct stages: obtaining approval, documenting it, linking it to the order or attaching it to the system.
claim.scope: Constraint of competing process accounts, without an assertion that a unique account or a particular failure stage has been established.

contract_question: Given the cited premises, observations, and transferred mechanism, does the claimed target conclusion follow at the strength and scope stated?

target.title: Supplier approval records
target.frame: A nonprofit requires documented approval before staff place supplier orders above an internal spending threshold. A quarterly review found that 14 of 90 sampled orders lack an approval attachment in the purchasing system. Approvals may also be recorded in meeting minutes or delegated-authority forms. The operations lead must prepare a defensible account of what happened and decide which records or process changes to pursue before the board review in three weeks. The internal rule is given; no legal conclusion is requested.

instrument.state: An internal structure cannot be sampled directly, but variations within it systematically alter the propagation of signals that cross it along many paths.
instrument.operation: Measure signal travel behavior across many source-to-receiver paths, compare those observations with predictions from a candidate internal model, and iteratively adjust the model to reduce the discrepancies.
instrument.signal: The observed propagation times or waveforms differ from model predictions in spatially structured ways across the sampled paths.
instrument.inference: The pattern of discrepancies constrains a spatial model of internal properties that could have produced the observed propagation behavior.
instrument.limit: Sparse or uneven path coverage, measurement error, uncertain source locations, regularization choices, model assumptions, and non-uniqueness can create artifacts or allow multiple internal structures to fit the observations.

P001.text: Act on the sampled orders and the documentary traces linking approval decisions, order placement and purchasing-system records.

P002.text: The historical approval process is not directly observable; reconstruct it through multiple record paths.

P003.text: The packet establishes that 14 of 90 sampled orders lack purchasing-system approval attachments, but does not establish that approval was absent.

P004.text: Verify which orders exceeded the threshold and what the internal rule required at the time.

P005.text: Assume only provisionally that records can be linked and their dates interpreted reliably.

P020.text: Use the pattern of discrepancies to constrain competing accounts of where the process departed from its predicted route: obtaining approval, documenting it, linking it to an order, or attaching it to the system.

P025.text: Record paths may be sparse, uneven, dependent on copied material or affected by missing records, ambiguous identifiers, unreliable timestamps and uncertain approval origins.

P026.text: Standardizing all orders into one assumed workflow could conceal legitimate routes or manufacture apparent failures; retain exceptions and test assumptions.

P027.text: Multiple historical processes may produce the same surviving records.

P028.text: Do not infer a population failure rate from 14 of 90 without a defensible sampling basis, and do not make legal conclusions.

P029.text: Stop an individual inquiry when sufficient reliable evidence resolves the applicable rule or when identified sources are exhausted and the remaining uncertainty is documented.

P030.text: At the board deadline, report unresolved cases without forcing closure, assigning each a specific next evidence request and responsible owner.

P031.text: Preserve original records when adding links or annotations; any later approval or remediation must retain its actual date and must not be presented as prior approval.
